source.title: Pre-Training LLMs on a budget: A comparison of three optimizers
source.authors: Joel Schlotthauer; C. Kroos; Chris Hinze; Viktor Hangya; Luzian Hahn; Fabian Küch

record.file_problem: The paper text is present, but the figures are not rendered; numerical values shown only in figures are unavailable in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: It does not fit or test scaling laws, but it compares pretraining loss with downstream performance and compares architectures at a fixed target size, bearing on V6 and V4 by different measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper uses the Chinchilla scaling laws to motivate its approximately 2.7B-parameter, 60B-token setup, but does not sweep model size, tokens, or compute or fit scaling laws. It reports loss and downstream comparisons across optimizers, regimes, and architectures; only those comparisons that bear on tested versions are recorded. The µP width experiments select learning rates by training loss, not by testing loss scaling.
record.test_reason: This is an optimizer comparison at one fixed target size (2.7B parameters, 60B tokens). It uses the Chinchilla rule to choose that setup and never varies parameters, tokens or compute, so no result bears on any scaling-law version. The loss-versus-downstream ranking comparison is across optimizers at fixed scale, not downstream improvement with scale or with loss along a scaling curve, so it does not test V6. The GPT-2 versus LLaMA comparison changes normalization, activation, MLP and bias, not shape at fixed parameter count, and its size is unquantified, so it does not test V4. Both findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that all three optimizers land in approximately the same range. Lion converges fastest and uses the fewest GPU hours. Sophia reaches the lowest final losses, especially in multi-epoch GPT training. AdamW gives the best downstream accuracy. They add that repeating epochs can slightly help AdamW downstream, that LLaMA needed about twice GPT's learning rate, and that µP transfer works for Lion and Sophia under AdamW scaling rules.
record.recipe_differences: This is an optimizer comparison at roughly fixed model size and token count, not a scaling-law sweep or fit; the scaling-law work is used to motivate the target setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with optimizer, architecture, and data regime; the authors report that GPT generally outperforms LLaMA except with Lion, and that repeated epochs particularly benefit Sophia's loss results with GPT.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed scale (2.7B, 60B tokens, repeated-data regime), Sophia reached the lowest final loss while AdamW had the highest downstream accuracy. Lower pretraining loss across optimizers did not rank downstream performance. In the single-epoch regime, AdamW led on both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed model size and token count, pretraining loss differences between optimizers do not reliably predict downstream accuracy rankings.

fits_no_version.finding: At 2.7B parameters, GPT-2-style models generally had lower loss and higher downstream accuracy than LLaMA-style models, except with Lion, where LLaMA was better. Magnitudes are not given in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ranking of architecture families at fixed size depends on the optimizer used.

record.problems: The study reports no repeated random-seed runs, statistical inference tests, or confidence intervals. The authors state that compute limits prevented these. The supplied text does not render figure values, so the recorded comparisons rely on prose summaries rather than numerical results.
record.rows_left_out: Per-benchmark downstream values and plotted loss values are not extractable from the supplied text; the prose-level comparisons are recorded in r1–r4. Figures 1–5 contain the referenced plots.

untested.parts: No sweep over parameters, tokens or compute, and no power-law fit.
No extrapolation from small to large runs. The µP proxies are used only for learning-rate transfer.
Chinchilla's tokens-per-parameter allocation is assumed to set the 2.7B/60B budget, not tested.
No depth or width variation at fixed parameter count. Only two architecture families are compared, without magnitudes.
Repeated-data runs (5 epochs of 12B tokens) exist, but no power-law form is fitted in that regime.
No downstream-versus-scale or downstream-versus-loss curve. Only optimizer rankings at a single scale are compared.
No exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted.

record.verdict_notes: The text is internally inconsistent. The abstract says Sophia had the lowest training and validation loss overall, but Section 4.1 says AdamW had the lowest final losses in the single-epoch regime. Sophia leads only in the multi-epoch regime. The study uses Chinchilla (about 20 tokens per parameter) only to choose its budget. It uses a single seed, reports no confidence intervals, and figure values are not in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits or loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute sweeps.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
Only GPT-2 and LLaMA architectures at the approximately 2.7B target size are compared; the magnitude of architecture effects and a wide range of architecture configurations are not tested.
Repeated-data training is compared, but no power-law form is tested in repeated-data training or other modalities or regimes.
Tests loss/downstream correspondence across optimizer and training-regime comparisons, not downstream predictability across scale; no numerical loss-to-task relationship is fitted.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared.

rows.subject: GPT-2 2.7B optimizer runs (AdamW, Lion, Sophia)
rows.operation_detail: Compared final training and validation loss with downstream benchmark performance.
rows.measure: Relative ordering of final training/validation loss and downstream accuracy
rows.value: AdamW had the lowest final training and validation losses; AdamW also achieved the highest downstream accuracy across benchmarks.
rows.note: Qualitative optimizer-level comparison stated in the prose; per-benchmark numerical values are not available in the supplied text.
rows.check: This is an optimizer comparison at fixed scale (single epoch, GPT-2). AdamW is best on both final loss and downstream accuracy. That is loss and downstream agreeing across optimizers, not V6 (predictability with scale or with pretraining loss along scaling). No per-benchmark numbers are available in the text.

rows.subject: GPT 2.7B optimizer runs (AdamW, Lion, Sophia)
rows.operation_detail: Compared losses under repeated-data training with downstream benchmark performance.

conditions.value: five epochs over 12B tokens, totaling 60B tokens

rows.measure: Relative ordering of final loss and downstream accuracy
rows.value: Sophia achieved the lowest overall losses, particularly with GPT in the repeated-epoch regime; AdamW consistently achieved the highest downstream accuracy.
rows.note: The reported optimizer ranking for loss does not match the downstream-accuracy ranking.
rows.check: Repeated-data regime. Sophia has the lowest loss, especially with GPT, yet AdamW is best downstream. This is a loss/downstream ranking mismatch across optimizers at fixed scale, a different construct from V6. The subject should note that both GPT and LLaMA were run, and that the Sophia loss lead is stated mainly for GPT.

rows.subject: GPT and LLaMA 2.7B model runs
rows.operation_detail: Compared training dynamics and losses across the two architectures.

conditions.value: five epochs over 12B tokens, totaling 60B tokens
AdamW and Sophia; prose summarizes the general architecture trend

rows.value: The paper reports that GPT architectures generally outperformed LLaMA architectures, except with Lion.
rows.note: The prose gives a directional comparison but does not quantify whether the architecture-related loss differences are slight.
rows.check: GPT-2 versus LLaMA differ in components (norm, activation, MLP, bias), not in depth or width at fixed size, and the size of the loss gap is not given. This does not measure V4's shape effect.

rows.subject: GPT and LLaMA 2.7B Lion-trained model runs
rows.operation_detail: Compared training dynamics and losses across the two architectures.

conditions.value: five epochs over 12B tokens, totaling 60B tokens

rows.value: The architecture trend reversed with Lion, favoring LLaMA.
rows.note: The paper reports a reversal in relative performance but does not quantify its magnitude.
rows.check: Same issue as r3. The reversal under Lion is directional and unquantified, and it compares architecture families rather than shape.
